description:
About TrueContext

#CareersThatKickSaas! TrueContext offers a forms automation solution and a leading workflow management app. Our Support team is based in Ottawa, and this role extends our coverage into the European morning.


The role

When something breaks in a customer’s field operation, you are who they reach out to. TrueContext runs the forms, workflows, and data capture that thousands of field technicians depend on every day, so a stalled integration can leave a crew standing around a job site.

This role opens our support day. You will work remotely from Europe and support customers in every region, starting before our Ottawa team comes online. Many of the cases on your shift come from customers outside North America, but you will pick up whatever is in the queue. The role is blended by design: you pick up the ticket, reproduce the issue, and carry it to a fix yourself.

The Customer Success Manager owns the customer’s outcomes and the Account Manager owns the commercial relationship. You own the problem in front of you: quick acknowledgement, a real diagnosis, and an answer the customer understands. For many customers who reach us early in the day, you will be the first person they reach and the most visible evidence that we are dependable.


What you’ll do

  • Own the ticket, start to finish. Work the queue across email, portal, and phone for customers in all regions. Expect much of your volume to come from customers outside North America, though you will handle any case that comes in. Figure out what the customer is actually trying to accomplish, not just what they typed in the ticket, and stay with it through to resolution.
  • Diagnose the cause. Most of the job is diagnosis. Reproduce the problem, then narrow it:
    • Form behavior: conditional logic, repeatable sections, calculated fields, validation rules
    • Data Source and Data Destination failures: refresh schedules, mapping errors, payload formatting
    • API responses and integration logs, to work out whether the break sits with us, with the customer’s connected system, or in the configuration between them
    • Mobile issues on iOS and Android: offline sync, device performance, version mismatches
  • Fix it, or write it up. When it turns out to be a configuration choice, show the customer what to change. When it is a bug, write it up well enough that Engineering can act without three rounds of follow-up questions.
  • Hand off cleanly to the Ottawa team. Your shift overlaps with the start of the Ottawa team’s day at 8:00 AM Eastern Time. Use that hour to brief the team on open cases, escalations in progress, and anything that needs follow-up, so no customer has to repeat themselves.
  • Handle escalations and incidents. Escalate early rather than after a customer has run out of patience. Before the Ottawa team is online, you escalate to the Customer Support Manager and the Engineering on-call. Hand Engineering a reproduction path and the real business impact. During platform incidents early in the day, you will often be the first to spot the problem: raise it, keep affected customers posted, and close the loop with each one afterward.
  • Make the next ticket unnecessary. Recurring problems should end up as help articles and internal runbooks instead of repeat tickets. Keep the ticketing system honest while you are at it: accurate categories, current status, resolution notes someone else could follow.
  • Work alongside our AI agent. An AI agent answers common customer questions before they reach the queue, so the cases that come to you will more often be the ones that need real diagnosis. You will review conversations the agent hands off or gets wrong, flag gaps to the team, and keep the help articles it draws on accurate and current. Every article you fix makes the agent better at solving that problem on its own.
  • Be the early warning system. Support sees trouble before anyone else does. Pass ticket patterns and sentiment shifts to the Customer Success Manager and Account Manager so nobody is surprised at renewal. Same with Product: which parts of the platform generate the most friction, and the evidence to back it up.


How the team works

We share one clear standard for how we serve customers, and we teach it to everyone who joins. You will work closely with the Ottawa Support team, the Customer Success Managers and Account Managers, Product, Engineering, and our Salesforce admin.


How you will be measured

First 90 days

You work a typical ticket from first reply to fix without help: form logic, Data Destination failures, mobile sync. You run the morning handoff with the Ottawa team on your own.

6 months

Engineering acts on your bug reports without follow-up questions. You have turned recurring issues into help articles that the team and our AI agent use.

12 months

Your response times, resolution times, and customer satisfaction are at or above the team’s targets. You have flagged at least one ticket pattern that changed a customer plan or a product decision.


What you bring

  • 2 - 4 years in a technical support or similar customer-facing technical role at a SaaS company. More than anything, you can take a vague description of a problem and narrow it to a cause.
  • You are comfortable reading API documentation, inspecting a JSON payload, and interpreting error codes. Some exposure to REST APIs, webhooks, or integration platforms matters more than any particular tool on your resume. Low-code, mobile, or field service platforms are a bonus, as is supporting apps on both iOS and Android.
  • Strong hands-on experience working in Salesforce, ideally Service Cloud: you move through cases quickly, understand how cases, queues, and assignments fit together, and can build your own reports and list views. Salesforce is the backbone of our support operation, so you will help keep it running well: spot what is broken or slowing the team down, and bring clear, specific change requests to our Salesforce admin, who owns configuration changes.
  • Professional fluency in written and spoken English.
  • You can explain a technical cause to a non-technical user without making them feel small. You are organized, because this is a queue rather than one problem at a time, and you stay steady when a customer is upset and the answer is not obvious yet.
  • You work well remotely and independently, since much of your shift runs before the rest of the team is online.


Nice to have:

  • Salesforce administrator experience or certification, ideally in Service Cloud (case routing and assignment rules, flows, page layouts and fields, reports and dashboards).
  • Jira Service Management.
  • Familiarity with AI support agents or chatbots in a help desk.
  • Professional proficiency in a language other than English, such as French, German or Dutch.
  • A background in field service, construction, utilities, or another regulated industry.


Schedule and work setup

  • Shift: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM Eastern European Time. That is 1:00 AM to 9:00 AM Eastern Time for most of the year, so your day starts well before the Ottawa team comes online.
  • Handoff: A daily handoff with the Ottawa team when they start at 8:00 AM Eastern Time.
  • Training: For your first four weeks, your shift starts later so you overlap with the Ottawa team for about five hours of live training and shadowing: 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM Eastern European Time (11:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central European Time). Your regular shift begins on week five.
  • Work setup: A reliable high-speed internet connection and a quiet, private space for customer calls and video handoffs. We provide your laptop and the tools you need.
  • Team: You will work closely with the Support, Product, and Engineering teams virtually.
  • Coverage: Occasional weekend coverage may be needed depending on team availability.


Some extra benefits

  • Yearly wellness allowance
  • Great time off benefits (3 weeks of vacation + 2 True2ME days + 1 TrueCrewCares day)
  • Fully remote work, with the tools you need provided
  • Local statutory benefits through our Employer of Record partner

 

Ready to make an impact? Apply today.
